quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 meets our preferred position: Vendor IP indemnity covering Customer and its Affiliates, plus indemnities for breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/cooperation/control procedure; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies; and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to unmodified Customer material and Customer's own violation of law. Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims (21.3).

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: Preferred position met: we own Customer Data and Deliverables (with a Vendor assignment), Vendor retains only its pre-existing Vendor Technology subject to the perpetual licence in 13.2, no joint ownership is created, and feedback use is limited and non-attributed.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap is currently measured on "Fees", which Section 1.5 defines as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the cap is illusory and well below six months' actual spend. We have changed the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000; the mutual structure and the Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) remain outside the cap.

ops.newText: shall not exceed the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
ops.oldText: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim

proposal.summary: Fix the cap basis so it is measured on all amounts paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor.

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
rationale: The cap is mutual, indirect damages are mutually excluded and the Excluded Claims set in 21.3 matches our preferred carve-outs (including that payment obligations are not damages). However the cap base is illusory: "Fees" is defined in 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the ceiling is far below six months' actual spend — walk-away territory. Redline changes the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Preferred position met: free Customer assignment to Affiliates and successors, Vendor assignment (including by change of control) requires our consent and never to a competitor, and Section 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, repricing or suspension on our change of control.

quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on us; Section 2.1 confirms we pay only for Services ordered and Section 12.3 expressly preserves our right to engage any supplier.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; 15% of annual Fees per week for a late invoice is punitive and unenforceable in substance. We have replaced it with customary late-payment interest on undisputed amounts.

ops.newText: 7.7 If an undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law. Customer is not liable for liquidated damages or penalties.
ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

proposal.summary: Delete the customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment and replace with simple late interest.

quote: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on Customer accruing weekly at 15% of annual Fees, triggered by a ten-day delay — a penalty running against us and outside even the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees). Redline replaces it with customary late interest on undisputed amounts.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes
rationale: Preferred position met: the grant expressly covers Affiliates and contractors, paid-up/embedded licences are perpetual and irrevocable (13.2), licence rights transfer to Affiliates and successors (13.3), and suspension is limited to material uncured breach after notice and cure.

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer; Section 12.3 expressly confirms the point. The only competitive restraint (12.4) binds Vendor, which benefits us and is not flagged.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: Preferred position met: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice (Section 29.4) with a refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination fee, and Vendor has no convenience right during the term (its rights are limited to breach and insolvency).

quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer.
rationale: Preferred position met: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems or unrelated data.

quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, and no arbitration — exactly our preferred position.

quote: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The only MFN runs in our favour (Vendor-granted best pricing), and Section 12.3 confirms we give no most-favoured-customer commitment. No redline; we keep the Vendor-granted MFN.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: No minimum commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall exposure; Section 7.1 also bars unstated minimum-use charges. This matches our preferred position.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No non-solicit or no-hire binds Customer anywhere in the document; Section 12.3 expressly negates any no-hire commitment. This matches our preferred position.

quote: Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Preferred position met: 12-month automatic renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out (extended if the 60-day Vendor reminder is not sent), and renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
rationale: Preferred position met and slightly better than it: six months' transition assistance at expiring (not then-current) rates, Customer Data returned within thirty days in a documented machine-readable format with no fee-dispute hostage, and certified deletion only after we confirm successful return.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Preferred position substantially met: professional/workmanlike standard, 90-day Deliverable conformance plus term-long hosted Services conformance, compliance with law and no malicious code, and a re-perform/repair/replace remedy escalating to termination and refund; the disclaimer in 19.5 expressly does not cut back the express warranties.

quote: commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
rationale: All preferred lines and limits are present (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation), maintained for the term plus one year, with certificates on request and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liability.
